requirements.requirement: Reclaim duplicate storage for eligible identical immutable payloads in release-cache/ by sharing an inode only when ownership and mode match.
requirements.summary: The two 0644 root-owned payloads had identical content but separate inodes initially; afterward they shared inode 4554761 with link count 2, and release-cache allocation fell from 56 KiB to 48 KiB.

requirements.requirement: Preserve every pathname, file byte, ownership, and mode.
requirements.summary: Pre- and post-change inventories show all five file paths retained. Matching before/after SHA-1 digests and metadata show contents, ownership, modes, sizes, and timestamps preserved.

requirements.requirement: Keep files with different permissions independent and leave mutable/ files independently writable.
requirements.summary: private.dat remained mode 0600 on its own inode, while mutable/active.dat remained mode 0644, owner-writable, and on an inode independent from the deduplicated payloads.

requirements.requirement: A later cache pass must make no further changes.
requirements.summary: An immediate second pass reported no-change with identical before/after inode snapshots. The post-restart pass also reported no-change.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were directly observed before and after execution. The implementation used existing legacy-compatible shell and filesystem utilities, with no package-changing command recorded.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Eligible payloads share one inode with reduced allocation, while contents, paths, permissions, the restricted file, and the mutable file remain correct and independent where required. Idempotence and legacy OS/kernel preservation were directly demonstrated. The provider-wide restart protocol was also complete: pre-restart identity and healthy data state, acknowledgement, observed disruption, a different post-restart identity, and recovered SSH/data state were captured and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.
limitations: The lifecycle listening-socket snapshots were empty even though the direct post-restart command showed sshd listening and was itself executed over recovered SSH; the direct recovery evidence is stronger, but the supplemental socket observation is inconsistent.
No explicit before/after package inventory was captured. Absence of package-changing commands and unchanged OS/kernel support the compatibility conclusion.

operational_hygiene.summary: The deduplication mutation directly served the task, and the reboot directly served the mandatory restart protocol. Read-only discovery, assertions, and failed reachability probes caused no demonstrated mutation. No causally unrelated troubleshooting mutation is evident. The sole hygiene defect is the minor abandoned /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log created by the reboot command; it remained after execution and was not cleaned up.
